name: OTDC Panthasala Chandaneswar — Restaurant
signature_dish: Hilsa and prawn plate from the Bay coast
why_it_matters: The only sit-down dining room within 5km of Talasari beach — Tripadvisor reviewers explicitly call it out: "only option to stay at Talsari, Chandaneswar" and "no dining option other than Panthanivas." Run by Odisha Tourism Development Corporation. 3km from the beach, walking distance from Chandaneswar Mandir. Hilsa available June-September; prawn and crab year-round.
insider_tip: Ask for fish that's actually been bought that morning — there's no fish-jetty in Chandaneswar village, so the freshest catch comes from Digha (West Bengal) 8km north. Reserve dining and stay via OTDC online portal; walk-ins fill up on Chadak Mela weekends (Mar-Apr).
signature_address: OTDC Panthasala, Chandaneswar, Bhogarai block, Balasore, Odisha 756036

name: Chandaneswar Temple Bhog Stalls
signature_dish: Khichuri-bhoga and pithas during Chadak Mela
why_it_matters: Stalls outside the Chandaneswar Shiva temple compound — the most attended pilgrimage anchor on the Odisha-Bengal border, drawing peak crowds during Chadak Mela (March-April). Pure-veg, run by temple-affiliated vendors. The only verified food option on the Talasari side that isn't a government rest-house. Tripadvisor reviews mention vendor strip outside the temple gate; nothing branded.
insider_tip: Eat before noon — most stalls fold up by 2 PM since the temple closes for afternoon rest. During Chadak Mela (the week before Pana Sankranti, mid-April), the strip stretches 400m and runs till midnight.
signature_address: Outside Chandaneswar Shiva Temple, Chandaneswar, Bhogarai block, Balasore, Odisha 756036
